criterion: Valid email, password, and display-name input creates one active account with a new opaque account identity, one private profile, an empty Todo collection, and an authenticated session.
A canonical email owned by an active account, invalid credentials, or an invalid display name refuses registration and creates no account, profile, Todo collection, or session.
A released email may register only as a new account identity with no relationship to the deleted account.
A matching canonical email and password starts a new owner-scoped session with the required inactivity and absolute deadlines.
Login neither replaces another valid session nor changes profile or Todo information.
Unknown email and wrong password return the same invalid-credentials outcome and create no session.
A valid unexpired session continues the same account identity without a password or authority expansion.
Successful continuation renews only inactivity expiry, never absolute expiry, and changes no product data.
A missing, unknown, expired, logged-out, or invalidated session cannot continue.
Current-session logout immediately revokes the presented session and prevents its reuse.
Current-session logout preserves every other valid session and all account and Todo data.
All-session logout revokes every session for the acting account, including the requesting session.
All-session logout preserves other accounts and all product data and permits a later eligible login.
Correct current password plus a different valid new password replaces the credential.
Successful password change rejects the old password and revokes every existing session, including the requesting session.
Wrong current password, reused password, or invalid new password preserves the credential and every session.
Recovery initiation returns one neutral public outcome for active, unknown, and released emails and returns no raw proof.
An active account receives a fresh proof only through its registered email channel, and issuance supersedes every earlier unused proof.
Only the newest unused proof before its 30-minute boundary can authorize recovery; missing, malformed, used, expired, and superseded proofs are refused neutrally.
Successful recovery atomically consumes the proof, replaces the password, and revokes every session; refusal changes none of those states.
Permanent account deletion requires the correct current password, and failed confirmation changes nothing.
Successful deletion atomically removes account, profile, every active and trashed Todo, every attached history entry, every recovery proof, and every session.
Deleted authority and data cannot reactivate or recover, while the canonical email is released only after deletion completes.
A released canonical email is available to registration only when no active account owns it.
Registration with a released email creates a new account identity, profile, empty Todo collection, and session.
No old password, proof, session, profile, Todo, history, or authority attaches to the new account.
A valid unexpired session is required for account management and every private profile, Todo, history, and trash capability.
Only registration, login, and neutral recovery initiation begin without a valid session and they disclose no private account information.
Absent or invalid authentication returns no protected information and changes no product or authority state.
An authenticated account can inspect and change only its own profile, Todos, trash states, and histories.
Todo ownership remains fixed and history derives the same owner throughout the retained lifecycle.
No sharing or transfer path exists, and an ownership mismatch reveals no target and changes no account.
A profile carries one current private display name distinct from email and account authority.
Changing display name leaves credentials, account identity, Todo ownership, and history ownership unchanged.
Every account has exactly one profile created and deleted with that account.
The profile relationship cannot transfer, share, detach, or become publicly discoverable.
Every Todo has the defined ID, title, optional description and dates, completion status, creation date, and content revision.
Todo ID is opaque, stable, unique across retained Todos, never reissued after deletion, carried by list and detail results, and distinguishes tasks with identical visible values.
Content revision begins at 1, increments exactly once per accepted content edit, and is preserved by every non-content action.
Optional values are independent calendar-date or text values and creation date remains immutable.
Each Todo belongs permanently to the account that created it and retains its ID through every retained state.
A Todo and its history cannot transfer, share, reassign, or detach.
Account deletion removes every owned Todo and all attached history regardless of state.
Every existing Todo has exactly one of incomplete or complete status and begins incomplete.
Content, soft-delete, and restore actions preserve completion status.
Completion is independent of availability and does not change content revision.
Every retained Todo has exactly one of active or trashed availability.
Active and trashed states expose only their defined list, detail, and change surfaces.
Availability is independent of completion and permanent deletion leaves no availability state.
Owner soft deletion changes one active Todo to trashed, records the most recent trash-entry time, and moves list visibility.
Soft deletion preserves ID, content, dates, revision, completion, owner, creation, and history and creates no edit-history entry.
A trashed or permanently deleted Todo cannot repeat soft deletion.
Owner restoration changes one trashed Todo to active and moves list visibility without replacing its identity.
Restoration preserves ID, content, dates, revision, completion, owner, creation, and history and creates no edit-history entry.
An active or permanently deleted Todo cannot restore.
Permanent deletion is available only for a trashed Todo and removes it and every attached history entry.
No ID, content, revision, completion, creation, ownership, detail, list, or history remains after deletion.
Permanent deletion is terminal, irreversible, and cannot repeat.
Each accepted content edit creates one entry with resulting revision, edit time, and all participating changed-to values.
An unchanged field is absent while an optional field cleared to empty is explicitly present.
Completion, soft deletion, and restoration never appear as content-edit entries.
Entry revisions are present, unique within one Todo, and establish accepted-edit order independently of timestamp ties.
Every history entry belongs to exactly one Todo and derives its account owner.
Soft deletion and restoration retain the same complete history.
Permanent Todo or account deletion removes every history entry in its ownership scope.
An authenticated account can view its one private profile and current display name.
Profile viewing exposes no other account identity or profile existence and changes no state.
Unauthenticated access returns no private profile information.
An authenticated owner can replace its display name with a valid value.
Successful profile editing changes only display name.
Invalid or other-owner profile editing is refused and preserves all account information.
An authenticated account can create a Todo from valid required title and independently optional description and dates.
Successful creation assigns a new opaque ID, permanent owner, creation date, active availability, incomplete status, and revision 1.
Creation produces no edit-history entry.
Invalid creation produces no Todo or history state.
Active browsing scopes by authenticated owner and active availability before filter, sort, and pagination.
Each list item carries ID, title, completion, optional dates, creation date, and content revision.
Supported completion filters and sort combinations apply with the specified defaults, null order, totals, and ties.
Unsupported pagination, filter, or sort input is refused without a partial interpretation or private leakage.
An authenticated owner can view an active Todo by ID with complete detail, revision, and availability.
Empty optional values remain distinguishable and viewing changes no state.
A trashed, absent, or other-owned ID returns no private Todo detail.
An owner edit identifies an active Todo and presents the expected current content revision.
An accepted edit changes only supplied differing content fields and increments revision exactly once.
The accepted edit atomically creates one history entry carrying the same resulting revision, edit time, and participating values.
Clearing an optional value is recorded explicitly while unchanged values are absent from the entry.
Invalid, no-op, state-ineligible, and ownership-ineligible edits preserve content, revision, and history.
A mismatched expected revision is a stale refusal that preserves the newer accepted state without leaking it across the unavailable boundary.
An owner can mark an active incomplete Todo complete.
A repeated complete request is a no-change success, while ineligible targets are refused privately.
Completion preserves ID, content, dates, revision, creation, availability, ownership, and history and creates no entry.
An owner can mark an active complete Todo incomplete.
A repeated incomplete request is a no-change success, while ineligible targets are refused privately.
Marking incomplete preserves ID, content, dates, revision, creation, availability, ownership, and history and creates no entry.
An owner can move an active Todo to trash and the same ID moves between list scopes.
Soft deletion preserves ID, content, dates, revision, completion, creation, owner, and history and creates no entry.
A trashed, absent, or other-owned target is refused and prior state remains unchanged.
An owner can traverse history for an active or trashed Todo by ID through bounded pages.
Pages order entries by accepted content revision descending and expose ID, current revision, totals, current page, and page size.
Traversing every page over unchanged history reaches every retained entry once without response truncation.
Each entry exposes resulting revision, edit time, and only participating content changes, never completion or availability events.
History viewing changes no state and absent or other-owned targets reveal no private information.
Trash browsing scopes by owner and trashed availability and orders newest trash-entry time first.
Each trash item carries ID, summary content, revision, creation date, and trash-entry time.
Trash uses bounded pages and totals without active filter or user-selected sort.
Unsupported pagination is refused and active or other-owned Todos never enter the result.
An owner can view a trashed Todo by ID with complete preserved detail, revision, trash time, and availability.
Trash detail identifies the same Todo and retains separately traversable complete history without changing state.
An active, absent, or other-owned target returns no private trash detail.
An owner can restore a trashed Todo and the same ID returns to active scope.
Restoration preserves content, revision, completion, creation, owner, and complete history and creates no edit entry.
Active, absent, or other-owned restore attempts are refused and prior state remains.
An owner can permanently delete a trashed Todo and all attached history.
Deleted ID has no list, detail, history, restore, edit, completion, or later deletion surface.
Active, absent, or other-owned permanent-delete attempts are refused and retained state remains unchanged.
Email trims outer whitespace, validates form, and compares without case distinction.
At most one active account owns a canonical email and duplicate registration changes nothing.
The same canonical identity applies to login and recovery while an invalid email cannot identify an account.
Every initial or replacement password contains 8 through 128 untrimmed characters with no character-class requirement.
Out-of-range passwords are refused and preserve account, credential, and session state.
Unknown email and wrong password return one indistinguishable login failure and create no session.
Repeated login failure reveals no credential condition and changes no product or authority state.
Password change requires current password and a different valid replacement while recovery requires a valid one-time proof.
Successful replacement makes only the new password valid and revokes every prior session.
Invalid proof or replacement preserves credential and every session.
Active-account recovery issues a fresh proof with at least 128 bits of unpredictable entropy only through registered email while public initiation remains neutral.
Issuance leaves only the newest proof eligible and supersedes every earlier unused proof.
An eligible proof is single-use before 30 minutes and is refused at or after the boundary.
Successful recovery atomically consumes proof, replaces credential, and revokes all sessions while any refusal changes none.
Concurrent completions with one eligible proof produce exactly one success and every other attempt observes a consumed proof.
Canonical uniqueness covers active accounts and release occurs only after complete permanent deletion.
Released email registration creates a new account identity.
No removed password, session, proof, profile, Todo, or history can authenticate or attach after email reuse.
Display name trims outer whitespace and accepts 1 through 100 remaining characters.
Duplicate display names across accounts remain valid and confer no relationship or authority.
Invalid registration or edit name is refused and an edit preserves the current name.
Title trims outer whitespace and accepts 1 through 200 remaining characters.
Description is independently optional and accepts at most 10000 characters.
Invalid creation or editing is atomic, and refused editing creates no history.
Start and due dates are independently optional and either may appear alone.
When both dates exist, due is equal to or later than start after all supplied changes.
An inverted resulting pair is refused and preserves both dates and history.
Active and trash pages are one-based with default page 1 and size 20.
Page size accepts integer values 1 through 100 and each page reports matching count and total pages.
Ownership, availability, and filter apply before totals and page boundaries; beyond-final pages are empty with correct totals.
Page below 1 or size outside 1 through 100 is refused.
Active filtering accepts exactly all, complete-only, and incomplete-only and defaults to all.
Filtering never admits trashed or other-owned Todos.
Every other filter value is refused.
Active sorting accepts creation newest or oldest, start earliest or latest, and due earliest or latest.
Missing start or due dates follow all dated Todos in both directions.
Every other sort field or direction is refused.
Active default is creation newest first and trash order is trash-entry newest first.
Equal start or due dates use creation newest then canonical Todo ID text in ascending code-point order.
Equal creation dates use canonical Todo ID text ascending and equal trash times use creation newest then the same ID order.
Complete deterministic order is established before pagination and repeats on unchanged input.
History pages are one-based with default page 1, default size 20, and accepted size 1 through 100.
Each history page reports entry count, page count, current page, and page size.
History orders unique accepted revisions descending, returns correct empty beyond-final pages, and refuses invalid bounds.
Bounded pages preserve complete unchanged-history traversal without truncation or duplication.
Only active Todos support normal detail, content editing, completion changes, and soft deletion.
Only trashed Todos support trash detail, restoration, and permanent deletion while history is available in both retained states.
State-ineligible and permanently deleted targets change nothing and expose no ineligible surface.
Requesting an already-current completion value on an owned active Todo is a no-change success.
Repeated completion preserves every Todo and history fact and creates no entry after ownership and state checks.
Content edit identifies the Todo, presents expected revision, and supplies at least one differing editable value.
A no-op edit is refused and creates no history.
Expected revision mismatch is stale and preserves the newer content, revision, and history.
Invalid content, wrong state, or ownership mismatch preserves content, revision, and history.
Concurrent valid edits with one current expected revision accept at most one edit and every other request becomes stale before changing content or history.
Every accepted content edit increments revision exactly one and creates exactly one matching immutable entry.
One multi-field edit keeps all changed-to values in the same entry and never changes earlier entries.
Completion, soft deletion, restoration, and refused edits create no content-history entry.
History remains immutable until terminal Todo or account deletion removes its scope.
Authenticated list, detail, history, and account views and changes contain only the acting account's information.
Cross-owner and absent private targets have the same unavailable outcome.
Unauthorized attempts reveal no existence or content and change no account or Todo state.
No capability makes private identity, profile, Todo, trash, or history public, shared, transferable, or assignable.
Accepted content, incremented revision, and exactly one matching history entry become visible together.
No accepted edit lacks history and no unaccepted edit produces history.
Every refused edit preserves content, revision, and history atomically.
Soft deletion atomically moves the same Todo and history from active to trash surfaces.
Restoration atomically moves the same Todo and history from trash to active surfaces.
Both transitions preserve ID, content, dates, revision, completion, ownership, creation, and complete history, and any failure leaves the complete prior state visible.
Permanent Todo deletion removes the trashed Todo and every attached history entry together.
Account deletion removes account, profile, all Todos, histories, proofs, and sessions together.
Completed deletion leaves no orphan or recovery path while refusal or failure preserves the full prior scope.
No response or log returns or records submitted passwords, raw recovery proofs, or password verifiers.
Password and recovery verifiers cannot recover submitted secrets and password verifiers are independently salted.
Raw recovery proof is exposed only through registered email and never through URL, analytics, or unrelated response.
Each session credential has at least 128 bits of unpredictability, names one session, and never appears in URL, log, or public response.

Production browser authority uses encrypted transport, is not exposed to unrelated origins through URL, referrer, message, or cross-origin response, and refuses unauthorized cross-origin mutation regardless of credential carriage.
Revoked, expired, malformed, and unknown session credentials share the unauthenticated boundary and cannot continue.
A session expires after 7 days without continuation and no later than 30 days after issue.
Only continuation renews the idle deadline, ordinary operations move neither deadline, and either reached deadline refuses authentication without affecting another session or product data.
Registration and login issue fresh deadlines while logout, credential replacement, recovery, and deletion may revoke earlier.
Every named account, profile, active, history, and trash journey is keyboard reachable and operable in logical focus order.
Opening and closing menus or dialogs moves and restores focus correctly.
No journey traps focus, requires hover, or hides unavailable state until activation.
Controls have meaningful labels, visible focus, and field-associated corrective validation.
Named state and pagination outcomes are announced to assistive technology without forced focus movement and reading structure remains logical.
Completion, availability, validation, destructive, and pagination meaning never relies on color alone.
Normal text meets 4.5:1 contrast; text at least 24 CSS pixels or 18.66 CSS pixels bold and meaningful focus and control boundaries meet 3:1.
Core journeys reflow at 320 CSS pixels and retain all content, controls, operations, and messages at 200 percent text zoom.
The measured fixture contains the specified 10000 active, 10000 trashed, and selected 100-by-100 history scale and covers every named read and state-changing operation.
After five warm-ups, twenty sessions issue five requests each with at most twenty in flight and nearest-rank read p95 is at or below 500 milliseconds.

Under the same schedule with independent eligible targets, every state-changing request is expected to succeed and nearest-rank p95 is at or below 750 milliseconds with no failure, leak, skipped mutation, or weakened bound.
Excluded overhead, pinned environment, fixture, runtime versions, warm-up, repetitions, percentile method, and raw samples are recorded separately.
Active, trash, and history responses contain no more than accepted page size with default 20 and maximum 100.
Collection totals do not require materializing the complete collection in one response.
Detail and mutation responses contain only the selected Todo and directly matching outcome rather than the account collection or complete history.
